# The Quran — North Frisian (Mooring) Draft

**DRAFT — NOT PUBLISHED**

A first-pass, engine-rendered draft translation of the Locked
English Master into North Frisian (ISO 639-3: frr) in the
**Mooring dialect only** (Bökingharde Frisian, Frasch, of the
Risum-Lindholm / Niebüll area). North Frisian has no single
standard and its dialects are not all mutually intelligible:
this is a Mooring text, honestly labelled as such, and is not
presented as readable as their own language by speakers of
Söl'ring, Fering-Öömrang or the other dialects. Prepared under
the ruling of Robert Tilford, 2026-11-27, as a gift draft for
the Mooring-speaking community: attribution requested,
translator rights retained, no claim of community invitation
or endorsement. Saterland Frisian and West Frisian are
different languages and were not touched or drawn on.

**Base and sources.** Every seated Mooring form is attested
for Mooring in open sources held at the desk: English
Wiktionary North Frisian entries via kaikki.org (CC BY-SA;
1,546 entries, of which 463 carry Mooring senses and 113 are
untagged pan-dialect entries; 3,685 Mooring inventory forms
after the dialect screen) and the LearnFrisian Mooring
wordlist (178 English–Mooring pairs; checked by its makers
against friesisch.net and Wiktionary, CC BY-SA 4.0). Bendsen's
*Die nordfriesische Sprache nach der Moringer Mundart* (1860,
public domain) was held as historical corroboration by fact
and citation only; its 1860 spellings were not seated as
modern forms. No form attested only for another North Frisian
dialect was seated. No complete Mooring Bible control exists;
the only complete North Frisian New Testament (Clemens, 1870)
is in Söl'ring, a different dialect, and was not used. That
absence is part of this draft's record.

**Honest status.** This draft has NOT been independently
checked and has NOT been published. It awaits a fresh
independent checker who did not build it. Of 6,236 verses,
6190 carry one or more visible GAP markers
(50826 markers, 5551
distinct English terms) where no attested Mooring form was
held: the gap was held open rather than filled with an
invented or borrowed word. The gaps include, prominently,
God, lord, heaven, angel, soul, spirit, mercy and sin — none
has a modern Mooring seat in the held inventories (Bendsen
attests God in 1860 spelling, Godd / Göd, as historical
corroboration only) — and a number of everyday function words
(for, who, on, by) that the held inventories likewise do not
attest for Mooring. The verified dictionary behind the seated
text holds 429 English–Mooring entries; 65 further
candidate entries failed verification and stand as GAPs
throughout.

**Plain-style devices, disclosed.** Verbs seat in their
dictionary (infinitive) form, with person and tense carried by
subject and time words; nouns seat in the nominative, with the
attested plural form where one is held and otherwise the same
dictionary form; articles and the genitive linker "of" seat as
zero, because Mooring articles are gendered and gender cannot
be assigned mechanically per noun without risking wrong gender
throughout; "you" seats in the singular form dü for all
persons. Personal names and scripture titles are carried in
the Master's forms.

**The Basmalah.** "Önj noome ⟦GAP: god⟧, ⟦GAP: beneficent⟧,
⟦GAP: merciful⟧." Önj (in) and noome (name) are attested
Mooring; God and both mercy names stand as GAPs for the reason
stated above, disclosed here rather than hidden. Surah 1:1 is
the Basmalah; every other surah except 9 carries it as an
unnumbered opening line (112 unnumbered lines).

**Novelty wording.** No "first" claim of any kind is made.
The scouting brief's bounded finding stands as: no North
Frisian Quran was found in the searches of 27 November 2026;
not found is not proven non-existent.
